newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Denktash says Clinton win is chance for Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Denktash says Clinton win is chance for Cyprus.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said on Wednesday that U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election presented a chance to solve the 22-year-old Cyprus dispute.

"This is an opportunity for Cyprus," Turkish Cypriot news agency TAK quoted Denktash as saying. He predicted Clinton would not side with the rival Greek Cypriots in the dispute on the eastern Mediterranean island.

"President Clinton is probably not going to come down on the side of the Greek Cypriots," he said. Denktash heads a self-proclaimed Turkish Cypriot state in northern Cyprus that is recognised only by Turkey.
The internationally-acknowledged Cypriot government is controlled by the Greek Cypriot majority.

"If there is a statesman who can tell the Greek Cypriots, 'You are not the government of the Turks. You are one of the two sides in Cyprus. You cannot ignore the effective and actual guarantee of Turkey,' it is Mr Clinton," Denktash said.
Turkey, which invaded Cyprus in 1974 after a Greek-engineered coup attempt on the island, maintains 30,000 troops in the north.
Peace initiatives by the U.N., European Union and the United States, including the Clinton administration, have all failed to bring the island's two communities together.
